articles.summary: Mid-green crop rows with flattened ring patterns, glossy fine sparkle like a lit field. Reads as a rich green sparkling metallic, like green glitter flake or grass seen from above, with soft light and dark clouds.
articles.what: Flattened agroglyph rings laid across a standing crop that all leans one way. Up close: Same crushed-glass facet mosaic (5-8 px cells) as Beacon Array, in emerald, forest and bright mint-green. Cell brightness drifts in soft broad cloudy patches of lighter and darker green, 100-200 px, with a slight diagonal lean. No rings or agroglyph shapes show. From a distance: Reads as a rich green sparkling metallic, like green glitter flake or grass seen from above, with soft light and dark clouds. Measured spec (average): metal 191, roughness 39, coat 47. Shine: high gloss. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, gt / sports car.

Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: the even grain covers every panel without a focal point
Hood and roof show the sparkle best in sun
White or yellow bold numbers read well; the small cells add a little grain but do not break big numbers.
Large soft shapes (fades, blocks): the grain is micro, so big graphics sit above
Pairs well with: black, yellow, white, chrome.
pitfalls: Not Beacon Array in blue: same fine grain, but here the colour is green and a cloudy light and dark drift shows
Not crop circles: no rings or geometry are visible in the render
Avoid: busy under numbers, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 191 (true metallic), roughness 39 (high gloss), clearcoat 47 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: busy under numbers, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large soft shapes (fades, blocks): the grain is micro, so big graphics sit above; bold stripes and number plates: stay crisp
Patterns to avoid: other glitter, flake or mosaic patterns: stacked grain turns to static; fine carbon or mesh: ruined by the cell grain

Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat on a stripe or number block: already high gloss, so only adds contrast if matte patches are used elsewhere; matte spec patch: a dull panel against the glittering gloss
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.summary: Near-black brown field packed with fine warm gold sparkle, like dust catching low light; semi-matte, no metal flake. A near-black brown car with a scattering of warm gold stars and a faint dusty haze; reads like bronze filings on black velvet.

From a distance: A near-black brown car with a scattering of warm gold stars and a faint dusty haze; reads like bronze filings on black velvet. articles.title: Deep Field: Deep Field
articles.summary: Very dark blue-black with a fine even scatter of pale white-blue sparkle; flat, matte, starfield-like. A black starfield with a scatter of white glints; the crosses read as sparkle points on a dark, slightly blue-black ground.
articles.what: Point the telescope at nothing for eleven days and this is what nothing turns out to be. Up close: Black field strewn with small white plus-sign stars, each a bright dot with thin horizontal and vertical arms, in a few sizes and brightness levels. Faint ghostly rings and arcs sit in the dark gaps. Cross-shaped, not round dots. From a distance: A black starfield with a scatter of white glints; the crosses read as sparkle points on a dark, slightly blue-black ground.
